## Upstream changes 19.5.1 -> 19.5.3

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no release notes could be read for this range, and the image registry lookup also failed, so this upgrade cannot be verified from any source; treat it as unreviewed rather than safe.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes — no notes were available to read (see below). This is not the same as a clean bill of health; it means the check could not be performed.

### Variables
- none found in the notes. The compose file pins the version as `GITLAB_IMAGE_VERSION:-19.5.1-ee.0` with a digest; moving to 19.5.3 requires updating both the tag and the sha256 digest in the `x-images` block (or overriding `GITLAB_IMAGE_TAG`/`GITLAB_IMAGE_VERSION` in `.env`) — this is a mechanical pin update, not a notes-driven variable change.

### Data and dependencies
- The compose file already runs PostgreSQL 17 and sets `max_locks_per_transaction=256`, `shared_buffers=256MB` — this is the current baseline, not something introduced by this upgrade, since GitLab's external-database guidance for raised lock tables already applies at 19.5.1.
- No companion-service version requirement from the 19.5.1→19.5.3 notes could be checked, because the notes are unavailable. If GitLab's notes for this range name a minimum PostgreSQL version, it cannot currently be confirmed against the compose file's pinned `postgres:17` — this alone would force NEEDS ATTENTION/DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED regardless of anything else, and must be checked by hand before proceeding.

### Before applying
- Take a GitLab backup before upgrading (standard practice for any GitLab version bump): `docker compose exec gitlab gitlab-backup create`, plus back up `/etc/gitlab` (the `gitlab-config` volume) since secrets and config live there.
- Manually check the official GitLab release posts for 19.5.2 and 19.5.3 (https://about.gitlab.com/releases/) and the GitLab UPGRADING/BREAKING_CHANGES documentation for this range, since neither could be retrieved here.
- Confirm whether 19.5.2/19.5.3 raise the minimum required PostgreSQL version beyond 17 before updating the pin.
- Update the `GITLAB_IMAGE_VERSION` default (and matching digest) in the compose file's `x-images` block to the correct 19.5.3 tag/digest — do not just bump the version string without the new digest.
- After upgrade, check `docker compose logs gitlab` for migration completion and confirm `/-/health` and `/-/readiness` respond before considering the upgrade complete.

### Notes read
- None. The release-notes source (gitlabhq/gitlabhq) returned 0 releases between 19.5.1 and 19.5.3, and no tag comparison was available. The registry lookup for the image configurations also failed (HTTP 404), so no differences could be measured there either. This review is based only on the compose file and `.env.example` as given.

## Upstream changes 2026.10.0 -> 2026.10.1

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no breaking change in the code paths this template exercises, but the behaviour change to timestamp formatting and the password-change session/token wipe can affect integrations and users without warning.

### Breaking changes
- **Timestamp format change on PostgreSQL** (this template runs PostgreSQL): "Timestamps include milliseconds. On PostgreSQL and SQLite, date and time values in API responses, webhook payloads and CSV exports now include milliseconds (`12:34:56.000+00:00`). Check integrations that read dates in a fixed format." Any downstream consumer (webhook receiver, CSV parser, external script) with a hardcoded time format will see this change.
- **Password change now revokes sessions/tokens**: "Changing your password deletes your API tokens and disconnects apps you authorized with OAuth." Anyone who rotates the admin password (e.g. via `NOCODB_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `.env`, which this template resets on every start) should expect existing API tokens and OAuth-connected apps to stop working.
- **MCP tool list expanded**: "The MCP server at `/mcp` now lists every tool. If Windsurf or VS Code Copilot shows too many tools, connect it again with the `/mcp-discovery` URL." Only relevant if MCP clients are connected to this instance.

### Variables
- none — no environment variable added, renamed or removed by this release's notes or by the compose/.env.example diff.

### Data and dependencies
- none introduced by this range. (The self-hosting note on `NC_ALLOW_LOCAL_EXTERNAL_DBS` and secure-attachments behaviour described under "Self-Hosting Notes" in 2026.10.1 describes existing flags already wired in this compose file — `NC_ALLOW_LOCAL_EXTERNAL_DBS` and `NC_SECURE_ATTACHMENTS` are already set — not a new requirement of this upgrade.)
- Companion services: Postgres 17 and Redis 7.4 are pinned in the compose file and nothing in the 2026.10.1 notes names a different required version for either, so no mismatch.

### Before applying
- Check any webhook consumer, scheduled export, or external script that parses NocoDB timestamps with a fixed-length format string; the added milliseconds (`.000`) will break strict parsers.
- If you plan to rotate `NOCODB_ADMIN_PASSWORD` around this upgrade, expect existing API tokens and OAuth app connections to be invalidated — re-issue tokens and reconnect apps afterward.
- No database migration, backup, or manual command is called for by the notes beyond the template's existing backup service.

### Notes read
- `2026.10.1` (release notes quoted above, including linked "Self-Hosting Notes") and `2026.10.0` (read only as the baseline per instructions, to confirm which items were already true and not new in this range).

## Upstream changes v3.8.8 -> v3.8.9

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no config/image-layer changes, but this release carries an irreversible, fleet-wide data migration that breaks compatibility with any older SiYuan client touching the same workspace.

### Breaking changes
- From the notes: "This release automatically migrates notebooks to the new document title mode and supports `/` in document titles." This migration runs automatically on first open with v3.8.9 and is not described as reversible.
- From the notes: "Before opening a workspace with this version, quit all older clients and upgrade every device that accesses or syncs the same data, including offline devices before they reconnect." If this host's workspace is also opened by desktop/mobile SiYuan clients outside this container, every one of them must be upgraded in lockstep, including devices that are currently offline.
- From the notes: "After migration, do not use older versions to open, edit, restore, or sync the same data: changes may be overwritten or lost and propagated through sync. Older clients rejecting some documents does not protect the entire notebook." A stale client (or a restore from an old client-compatible backup opened with an old client) can silently corrupt or lose data once this container has migrated the workspace.
- From the notes: "Check plugin compatibility before upgrading." Any installed plugins should be verified against v3.8.9 before this upgrade is applied.

### Variables
None. No variable was renamed, removed, or newly required by the notes, and the compose file / .env.example are unaffected.

### Data and dependencies
- No database/companion-service version requirement appears in the notes — SiYuan here uses its own embedded SQLite via the backups sidecar, not an external pinned engine, so the "unpinned companion version" rule does not apply.
- The notebook/document-title migration described above is the only data-affecting change, and the notes give no rollback path.
- The command-form requirement ("the kernel's `serve` subcommand with `SIYUAN_ACCESS_AUTH_CODE`") is already reflected in the current compose file's comment and command line — that is a pre-existing fact of the already-running v3.8.8 setup, not something this upgrade introduces.

### WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN
The registry comparison states the two image configurations are identical in `User`, `Entrypoint`, `Cmd`, `WorkingDir`, `ExposedPorts`, `Volumes`, `Healthcheck`, and environment. Nothing in the compose file (command, ports, volumes) needs to change for this upgrade; the only risk is the in-application migration described above.

### Before applying
- Before restarting the `siyuan` service on this host, make sure no other SiYuan client (desktop, mobile, or another container) is currently open against the same `./workspace` directory, and either upgrade them to v3.8.9 at the same time or keep them fully offline until they can be upgraded.
- Take a backup of `./workspace` before the restart — the `backups` sidecar already does this on its normal schedule, but trigger or confirm a fresh one immediately beforehand given the migration is one-way.
- Check any installed SiYuan plugins against v3.8.9 compatibility before upgrading, per the notes' explicit instruction.
- After upgrading, do not roll the image tag back to v3.8.8 (or open the workspace with any older client) if the migration has already run — per the notes this risks data loss/overwrite propagated through sync.

### Notes read
- v3.8.9 (2026-10-29) release notes, including the "Upgrade notice" section, read in full.
- v3.8.9 pre-releases (rc.1, beta.1–6, alpha.8–10) skimmed for completeness; they are superseded by the final v3.8.9 notes and introduce no additional points.
- v3.8.8 (2026-10-20) release notes, read as the stated baseline only.
- UPGRADING/BREAKING_CHANGES/CHANGELOG.md: not usable — the supplied content was only `Please see app/changelogs/ for details.`, which points elsewhere and was not provided.

## Upstream changes 7.1.3 -> 7.1.4

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no release notes exist for this image tag, so the actual code change behind 7.1.4 cannot be verified before applying.

No release-notes source was available: "(not available: WordPress publishes release notes on wordpress.org; docker-library/wordpress is the packaging and tags no versions)". That rules out a container-level change, but it says nothing about WordPress core/plugin behaviour inside the image, which is exactly what this version bump is for and exactly what cannot be checked here.

- none found in the notes — no notes were available to read. Treat this as unknown, not as confirmed-safe.

### Variables
- none — no renamed, removed, or newly-required variables indicated by either the compose file or .env.example for this bump.

- No new database version requirement, port change, path change, or irreversible migration is indicated by anything available for 7.1.3 -> 7.1.4.

- Check the WordPress core version bundled in `wordpress:7.1.4` against the WordPress.org changelog/security advisories yourself (https://wordpress.org/news/category/releases/) before rolling this out to production, since no packaging-level release notes exist for docker-library tags.
- Since the image's `User`, `Entrypoint`, `Cmd`, `Volumes`, `Healthcheck` and environment handling are unchanged between the two tags, no compose-file edits are required for this bump.

### Notes read
- No release notes could be read for this image. docker-library/wordpress does not publish per-tag release notes; WordPress core release/security notes live on wordpress.org and were not supplied. The only verified input was the registry image-configuration diff, which showed no behavioural differences in container-level fields.
